fixes.explanation: Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown Elizabeth, the baby's mother, great mercy, and they rejoiced with her. I think that's how you treat a friend's good news. You show up and you celebrate like it happened to you.

Luke says the opposite. Her neighbors and relatives heard the Lord had shown Elizabeth, the baby's mother, great mercy, and the verse says “…they rejoiced with her.” Rejoicing with her is what the text gives us, plain and simple.
Hold on, where did Grandpa come from? Luke never mentions a grandfather in this verse. He says they were going to name the baby after his father Zechariah, the baby's dad.
Luke doesn't mention an uncle anywhere in this scene. He says they were going to name the baby after his father Zechariah. The name on the table was the dad's name.

That's right, she doesn't agree. When they were going to name him Zechariah, his mother Elizabeth replied, “No! He shall be called John.” She starts with “No!” and then gives the name. I'd say she'd made up her mind.
After her “No!” she says, “He shall be called John.” The text gives just the name. That's the name in verse 60.
Samuel was a prophet (1 Samuel 3:20), and I'd have grabbed that name too. But Elizabeth says, “He shall be called John.” Samuel doesn't get a mention in this scene. Great name, different baby.
They tell her, “There is no one among your relatives who bears this name.” That's what they point out about John. It's about her relatives, and that's all they say here.

Zechariah asks for a tablet and writes his answer. He can't speak, so writing is how he gets it across. I went quiet for a long stretch in the back of a junk drawer, and a tablet would've been handy. It's a little slower than talking, but it gets the job done.

A staff is good for walking, but that's not what Zechariah asks for. Luke says he asked for a tablet, and then he wrote his answer on it. You can't write a name with a walking stick, at least not neatly.
He writes, “His name is John.” That's the same name Elizabeth already gave. And Luke says they were all amazed. The mom said it and the dad wrote it, and both land on John.
Luke doesn't say he questions anybody. When his tongue is released, he begins to speak, praising God. Praise is the first thing the verse says he does.
Nice thought, but the verse says he began to speak, praising God. It doesn't mention him blessing the neighbors. What it names is praise to God.
Good guess, since the name has just come up. But Luke says they asked, “What then will this child become?” That's the question the text gives them, and it's about the child.
Aaron was Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), so I get why he came to mind. But the verse says the horn of salvation is raised up “…in the house of His servant David…” The house here is David's.

Joseph was one of Jacob's sons (Genesis 37:2), and I see why he'd come to mind. But Zechariah says the oath was sworn “…to our father Abraham…” Joseph isn't in this verse at all. Abraham is the name Zechariah gives.
No, Zechariah doesn't say that. He says deliverance from hostile hands comes “…that we may serve Him without fear…” The word is fear, not king.

Building a house isn't part of John's assignment here. Zechariah says John will go on before the Lord “…to prepare the way for Him…” That's the job the verse gives him. Hammers can stay in the toolbox.

Zechariah says the Dawn will visit “…to shine on those who live in darkness and in the shadow of death…” I spent years in the dark at the back of a junk drawer, so I know light means a lot when you've been in one. That's who this light is for.

Luke says the child grew and became strong in spirit, and that he “…lived in the wilderness until the time of his public appearance to Israel.” So the wilderness is the place the verse gives for those years. After that comes his public appearance to Israel.
Luke doesn't put John in a city. He says the child “…lived in the wilderness until the time of his public appearance to Israel.” The wilderness is the place the verse names.
Luke doesn't say village. He says John “…lived in the wilderness until the time of his public appearance to Israel.” The wilderness is the place the verse names.
